full_judgment: 2. Respondent No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Title Suit against the appellant and respondent Nos. 2-5 for declaration of his title to the property in schedule annexed to the plaint and confirmation of possession therein and alternatively recovery of khas possession of the same. The plaint case is that, respondent No. 4 Rabindra Kumar Dey had purchased the suit land from the original owner, the Eastern Commercial Bank Ltd in the benami of his elder brother respondent No. 3 Birendra Kumar Dey who did not pay any consideration, by registered kabala dated 24-8-44 AD as he was indebted to many persons at the relevant time. Rabindra Kumar raised structures and let out the same to monthly tenants. Rabindra paid rents and taxes in the name of his brother Birendra Kumar and after he left this country Rabindra got his own name mutated in the settlement papers and in the municipality and ever since paid rents and taxes in his own name. The Government realised rent from Rabindra who paid up the certificate dues in Certificate Case No. 28330 of 1960-61. Rabindra''s brother Birendra had sworn an affidavit on 7-5-64 before the Presidency Magistrate, Calcutta, declaring that he was simply a benamder of Rabindra Kumar who was the real owner of the property. Rabindra sold the property to respondent No. 1 for a consideration of Rs. 15,000.00 by a registered kabala dated 20-11-63 AD. Respondent No. 1 after purchase mutated his name in the office of the Government and the municipality, and accordingly, paid rent and taxes. Respondent No. 1 filed suits for ejectment of monthy tenants and at this stage, the tenants set up one Asmat Ali who filed an application before the Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property (L&B), Comilla praying for taking lease of the same as enemy property whereupon enemy property Case No. 274 of 1969 was started and after enquiry the Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property by his order dated 21-4-69 held that the suit property was not an enemy property. But subsequently, the tenants of the plaintiff managed to influence the Assistant Custodian and obtained an order dated 5-5-69 behind the back of respondent No. 1 declaring the suit property as enemy property. On coming to know about the aforesaid order respondent No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 263 of 1969 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Comilla challenging the legality of the order dated 5-5-69 but the suit was withdrawan and Writ Petition No.177 of 1969 was filed for speedy relief. The Rule in the Writ Petition was discharged on 3-6-76 as not maintainable. Thereafter respondent No. 1''s Civil Petition for leave to appeal was also dismissed on 24-11-76. During the pendency of the aforesaid Writ Petition respondent No. 1 instituted the instant suit.
